stories.title: Montana High School Softball Player Discovered Long-Lost Sister on Opposing Team
stories.label: people
stories.summary: During a softball game in Montana this August, a teenage player found out that a girl on the opposing team was actually her biological sister. Samantha Rensvold, who was adopted, had been searching for family connections, and this chance meeting on the field brought two sisters together after years apart. The two teams and families were stunned by the coincidence, turning an ordinary game into an emotional reunion. It's the kind of real-life surprise that feels almost too good to be true, but it truly happened. Stories like this remind us how connected we all can be, even across state lines and years of separation.
stories.why_good: A heartwarming, true family reunion that happened by chance, bringing joy to two sisters and their families with zero political content.

stories.title: Italian Bio-methane Plant Comes Online, Providing Renewable Gas to Over 3,000 Homes
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: A new biomethane plant has switched on in southern Italy, turning farm waste into clean natural gas. It will supply renewable energy to more than 3,000 homes in the region. By making gas out of agricultural leftovers instead of fossil fuels, the plant will cut about 9,000 tons of carbon dioxide every year. It's a nice example of turning waste into something genuinely useful for both people and the planet.
stories.why_good: A real, operating facility that cuts emissions and powers thousands of homes with renewable energy made from waste.
